summary:
Earth Information Jukebox transforms complex NASA satellite visualizations into an interactive, multi-sensory 3D experience. Inspired by the scientific curiosity of Project Hail Mary and Outer Wilds, users awaken inside an orbital station and use an acoustic wave-scope to scan Earth and detect 10 real planetary anomalies from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS)—including global CO₂ emissions, atmospheric rivers, urban night lights, ocean currents, and forest canopy heights.

Instead of relying solely on static charts, our real-time sonification engine translates physical variables (such as pixel intensity, thermal gradients, and aerosol concentrations) into dynamic music and soundscapes via the Web Audio API. Players complete step-by-step guided analytical missions at each station to earn stars and unlock the 3D Causal Museum, where animated energy pulses reveal how Earth’s climate, biosphere, and human activity interconnect as a single living system.
details:
### What It Does & How It Works

Earth Information Jukebox is a browser-based 3D scientific exploration and data sonification platform built around 10 real Earth observation datasets from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS).

1. Orbital Exploration (The Wave-Scope): From an interactive 3D cockpit, users rotate around Earth (Q/E) and activate an acoustic scanner (Spacebar). As the reticle approaches an anomaly, static noise clears into generative musical harmonies mapped to that phenomenon.

2. Interactive Analytics Stations & Guided Missions: Selecting a signal opens an analytical console featuring the actual NASA SVS visualization alongside a real-time HTML5 Canvas data sampler, luminance histogram, and Web Audio synthesizer. Users isolate atmospheric layers, scrub through multi-year timelines, and freeze frames to pinpoint critical thresholds through sequential step-by-step guided missions.

3. The 3D Causal Museum: Unlocking discoveries opens an interactive 3D knowledge network behind the cockpit. Clicking any causal link animates energy particles flowing between phenomena (e.g., Night Lights -> Global CO₂ -> Ocean Currents) to visually explain Earth-system feedback loops.

### Impact & Creativity

Satellite datasets are vital for understanding climate change, yet their complexity often creates a barrier for students and the general public. By combining narrative game design, visual step-by-step scaffolding, and real-time audio sonification, our project makes Earth science intuitive, accessible (including screen-reader support and reduced-motion modes), and emotionally engaging—allowing users to literally hear the pulse of our planet.

### Tech Stack & Architecture

- Frontend & 3D Rendering: React 18, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber & @react-three/drei).

- Real-Time Audio & Sonification: Web Audio API, Tone.js, custom procedural noise and harmonic synthesizers.

- Data Sampling & Visualization: HTML5 Canvas 2D pixel-level telemetry extraction, custom histograms, and GitHub Pages CI/CD deployment.

- Source Code Repository: https://github.com/stella5555/DevDevu
